Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Dana (Head of ML, Ergo), Tom (Platform), Marta (CISO), Jared (Product)

Summary (auto): Discussed pilot scope: 100M tokens/month target, interactive chat with 512 token context, target 95th percentile latency ~200-250ms, cost target ~0.0006 per token or lower, explore hosted first with plan for Dedicated if needed. Action items captured.

[00:00] Aisha: ok hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick intros — we are Aisha (account exec), Marco (se) and Lena on the eng side. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Dana: good, thanks. quick background — we're building an internal conversational assistant for consultants, lots of short sessions but some long context threads, main ask is cost predictability and data controls.
[00:14] Tom: yep and platform side we worry about egress, VPC, and predictable throughput during spikes.
[00:18] Marta: and from security, SOC2 is table stakes, also KMS for customer data and we have residency in eu-west.
[00:23] Aisha: great, that's helpful. Marco, can you frame the basic economics and deployment options?
[00:27] Marco: sure. so at a high level Redwood offers hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated private pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem options) for stricter controls. Pricing components people care about are per-token unit cost, any reserved capacity commitments for Dedicated, and then operational levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization choices.
[00:44] Dana: can you unpack batching? we see it mentioned but not sure how it affects latency vs cost.
[00:48] Marco: yeah totally. continuous batching groups requests across a short window and amortizes the cost of a forward pass across many requests — so tokens per GPU sec goes up and cost per token goes down. downside is you add a batching delay (typically a few ms up to tens of ms) — we tune batching windows to meet your SLO. for interactive chat with 512 contexts, you can still get good batching if request arrival rate is consistent.
[01:15] Tom: what's the typical batch size you'd expect for our load? we gave a baseline of 100 concurrent users, avg 2 messages/minute.
[01:20] Marco: rough math — that arrival pattern could give you per-second arrivals enough to fill modest batches, maybe 8-16 on average; but we'd simulate. more important is prefix/KV cache reuse — if many conversations share prefixes (system prompt + user instructions) the KV cache avoids re-computing the early layers which is huge for cost and latency.
[01:39] Dana: how big is the delta with caching on a chat workload?
[01:42] Marco: it varies but typical wins are 20-60% token-cost reduction for chat when cache hit rates are high, and tail latency improves because early tokens are pulled from cache rather than computed. for very high reuse patterns you can see more.
[01:56] Marta: is KV cache available on Hosted? any data leakage concerns?
[01:59] Marco: yes hosted supports caching and Redwood segregates tenant caches. for enterprise customers we can also run Dedicated with customer-isolated caches or Private where your KV never leaves your VPC. we can map to your KMS strategy as well.
[02:15] Jared: ok on price numbers — we modeled ~100M tokens/mo; what price band should we expect on hosted vs dedicated?
[02:21] Aisha: I'll be candid: hosted per-token list pricing is higher than deeply committed Dedicated, but Hosted includes management, autoscaling, and no infra ops. for your volume, Dedicated with a moderate commit will likely lower unit costs by 20-40% depending on batchability and cache hit. we'll send a modeled spreadsheet.
[02:37] Dana: can you show an example calc? we target 0.0006/token — is that realistic?
[02:42] Marco: 0.0006 is in the realm of possibility if you get good batching and caching and choose a quantized model variant. for example, with 100M tokens and 50% cache hit, plus batching gains and a quantized 7B-ish model on Dedicated, your blended unit could approach that. but with hosted and no commit, you'll likely see 0.0009-0.0012/token. again these are estimates — we need your exact prompt lengths, hit rates, and arrival patterns to be precise.
[03:09] Tom: network costs? if we use Hosted in eu-west does egress bite us?
[03:13] Marco: network egress is typically small for token streams, but if you stream a lot of embeddings or large attachments it's something to consider; for Private/VPC, egress to your systems is internal.
[03:22] Dana: what's the pilot look like? we want to test economics and verify performance.
[03:26] Aisha: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: seed with a small dedicated capacity or hosted with a tailored config, run a benchmarking harness with your prompt set, measure cost and latency, then decide whether to move to Dedicated or Private. SOW includes success metrics: target 95th pct latency and unit cost thresholds.
[03:39] Marco: technically we'll instrument token-level telemetry and do a shadow run of your traffic. we'll also test batching windows and cache TTL to show sensitivity.
[03:46] Marta: for the pilot we need to pre-check the compliance posture — can you share SOC2 certs and the KMS integration docs?
[03:52] Lena: yes we have SOC2 and ISO docs; we also have a Private option with customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. we'll attach the pack.
[03:59] Jared: curious about fallback behavior if capacity is constrained — do you have model variant fallback?
[04:03] Marco: yes. Redwood supports policy-based routing — we can route by latency/cost/availability. fallback to a smaller model or quantized variant preserves availability at lower cost. we can make that automatic in a rollout policy.
[04:15] Dana: one concern is the user experience — we need predictable 95th pct for interactive users, can't have long tails. how do you keep the tail tight while using batching?
[04:24] Marco: common approach is multi-tiering: reserve a small fraction of Dedicated pool for low-latency fast-path (smaller batch window) and let the rest run cost-optimized batching. you can also use cache priming and pre-warm sessions. that typically keeps the tail in bounds.
[04:40] Tom: timeline — we have an internal procurement freeze mid-October; we'd like pilot to run mid-September to mid-October. is that feasible?
[04:47] Aisha: yes that's tight but doable — we can kick off hosted pilot next week and switch to a small Dedicated pool if you want reserved capacity. I'll get the SOW out by Friday.
[04:56] Marta: about residency — we need data to remain in eu-west for storage and logs, is that doable?
[05:01] Lena: yes; Hosted has region selection and we can restrict logs/retention; for stricter residency regarding caches and ephemeral data, Dedicated or Private gives stronger guarantees.
[05:12] Dana: do you support SSO/SAML and per-route RBAC?
[05:16] Aisha: yes SSO/SAML and RBAC are part of our enterprise feature set. we can show console screens in the next call.
[05:22] Tom: what's the expected engineering lift for VPC Private? we may have to engage infra teams.
[05:27] Marco: Private requires some infra setup — VPC peering or private endpoints plus a small on-prem agent if you're air-gapped. typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks with infra availability; for pilot, hosted or Dedicated avoids that up-front lift.
[05:41] Jared: are there any hidden costs around burst capacity?
[05:44] Aisha: bursts are handled with autoscaling in Hosted but large bursts can cause short-term higher bills; Dedicated has burst policies and committed burst allowances; we'll surface those in the pricing sheet.
[05:56] Dana: ok, so immediate asks from us: confirm pilot token target (we think 100M), confirm SLOs (95th 250ms), list security docs.
[06:03] Aisha: perfect — we'll send pilot pricing and a short SOW that ties to those metrics. Marco will also run a draft perf model with your 512-token chat numbers and different cache hit scenarios.
[06:12] Marta: one last clarifying Q — if we move to Dedicated later, what's the migration path? downtime?
[06:16] Marco: migration is usually non-disruptive; models are the same API. we can route traffic to Dedicated gradually and use rollouts/canaries. no hard downtime if planned.
[06:26] Dana: great. thanks all.
[06:28] Aisha: thanks — recap next steps: Aisha send SOW/pricing, Marco perf doc, Marta sends cert/KMS reqs, Dana confirms volumes. we'll reconvene once those are in.
